q: Mahomed Khan, disgusted at the authority assumed by his wuzzeer, and incensed at the affront he had offered or permitted towards the royal family, dispatched his son Camrim to Herat, with orders to seize the city and the wuzzeer, if possible.
1825, James Baillie Fraser, Narrative of a Journey Into Khorasan, page 36:
‘We wuz talkin’ and the monk got loose, and she sent me off to catch him.’
1932, Delos W. Lovelace, King Kong, published 1965, page 64:

e: From "who's a...", as in "who's a pretty boy?" etc.
q: Oh, Betty — I suppose I'll have to go in to see you. That Doctor Holt says not to, in his book — but I don't care. He never was a mother! (She enters nursery.) Betty! Betty, my darling, oh, you wuzza wuzza wuzza!
Patti scooped up the new cat. She put her nose against its nose and cooed, "Wuzza, wuzza, wuzza, her's a pussycat and needs love, doesn't her? Somebody so mean to throw you out. […]
2008, Bethany Campbell, Amarillo by Morning, page 148:

“How do you know the cat's name?”
“Katie told me,” Pete said without looking up. “Who's a wuzza wuzza wuzza? Hey? Who's a wuzza wuzza woo.”
Jack rolled his eyes. “I hope you're not like that with Katie. She seems like a tough girl.”
